MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY OCTOBER — TERMLY EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Marketing? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Marketing.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Marketing.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Marketing.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Marketing.

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Taxonomy 1.2 Fish Physiology 2.0 Aquaculture 2.1 Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvest? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Taxonomy 1.2 Fish Physiology 2.0 Aquaculture 2.1 Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvest.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Taxonomy 1.2 Fish Physiology 2.0 Aquaculture 2.1 Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvest.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Taxonomy 1.2 Fish Physiology 2.0 Aquaculture 2.1 Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvest.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Taxonomy 1.2 Fish Physiology 2.0 Aquaculture 2.1 Fish cage 2.2 Fish Harvest.

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish cage? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Fish cage.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish cage.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish cage.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish cage.

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Harvesting and Post- Harvest Handling? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Harvesting and Post- Harvest Handling.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Harvesting and Post- Harvest Handling.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Harvesting and Post- Harvest Handling.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Harvesting and Post- Harvest Handling.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Value Addition 2.4 Fish Marketing 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Fundamentals of? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Value Addition 2.4 Fish Marketing 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Fundamentals of.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Value Addition 2.4 Fish Marketing 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Fundamentals of.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Value Addition 2.4 Fish Marketing 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Fundamentals of.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Value Addition 2.4 Fish Marketing 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Fundamentals of.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Physiology? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Physiology.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Physiology.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Physiology.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Physiology.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fundamentals of Fisheries Management? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fundamentals of Fisheries Management.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fundamentals of Fisheries Management.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fundamentals of Fisheries Management.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Fundamentals of Fisheries Management.

14. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fishing gears and Methods Page 12 of 33 1 STRAND 1.0: FISH BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY S? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fishing gears and Methods Page 12 of 33 1 STRAND 1.0: FISH BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY S.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fishing gears and Methods Page 12 of 33 1 STRAND 1.0: FISH BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY S.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fishing gears and Methods Page 12 of 33 1 STRAND 1.0: FISH BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY S.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fishing gears and Methods Page 12 of 33 1 STRAND 1.0: FISH BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY S.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Value Addition? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Value Addition.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Value Addition.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Value Addition.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Value Addition.
